**MEMORANDUM**

To support your upcoming briefings, introducing a central business district congestion charge offers a powerful tool to alleviate gridlock, improve air quality, and generate sustainable funding for our transport network. For the scheme's design, I recommend exploring variable peak-hour pricing (e.g., $10–$15 during rush hours), combined with strategic exemptions for emergency vehicles, transit, and potentially discounted caps for low-income zone residents. Crucially, ring-fencing all net revenues to fund highly visible public transit and active mobility upgrades will be our strongest lever for securing public buy-in. On the risk front, we must anticipate intense political pushback from suburban car-commuters and local business owners who may fear decreased foot traffic. The most significant caveat to proactively address in your messaging is the equity concern for low-income drivers lacking viable transit alternatives; ensuring our exemption design explicitly mitigates this will keep the policy politically viable.
